subject.title: [Feature]:Support per-agent command lanes for multi-agent deployments

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in scheduler/config surface for per-agent or per-group foreground command lanes, and what default plus aggregate-cap semantics should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix creates a public config and scheduler contract across agent, channel, hook, browser, and subagent surfaces; automation should not choose that product boundary.

options.title: Design opt-in core lane policy
options.body: Keep main as the default, add maintainer-approved per-agent or per-group foreground lane config, and require aggregate cap, trusted config, docs, and tests.

options.title: Defer to narrow lane surfaces
options.body: Let hook, browser/channel, and subagent lane proposals proceed independently without a top-level per-agent foreground contract yet.

options.title: Document separate gateways
options.body: Keep foreground replies on the shared main lane and recommend separate gateway deployments for heavy agent groups.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in core lane policy
recommendation.body: Keep main as the default, add maintainer-approved per-agent or per-group foreground lane config, and require aggregate cap, trusted config, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal runs through the concurrency resolver, gateway lane setup, and embedded-agent lane behavior that define this scheduler contract.
